cards.title: Market volatility: Investing strategies for volatile markets | Fidelity
cards.thesis: Volatility-driven regimes favor dynamic risk budgeting and optionality leveraging, with a clear emphasis on the interplay between rates / central banks and price-discovery frictions.
cards.whyItMatters: As volatility persists, portfolio construction must adapt to regime shifts in rates while preserving liquidity and downside protection, potentially redistributing beta sensitivity toward options-like exposures.
cards.marketReadThrough: Expect incremental shifts in hedging posture by institutions; potential demand for vol-control strategies and cross-asset hedges as central bank narratives wrestle with growth and inflation.
cards.variantAngle: Translates a general volatility framework into a regime-based lens that links rate expectations to hedging costs and dispersion dynamics.

Reuters reported that over 80% of S&P 500 companies beat expectations as of last week. First quarter earnings are set to climb by over 25% year-over-year. Chipmakers have been especially influential. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is up over 100% since the end of March, while Intel (INTC) has nearly tripled to surpass it’s previous all-time high in the dotcom boom. While the technology sector has been a big driver for the market, up 16% YTD, other sectors have also contributed. Geopolitical conflict intensified, oil prices spiked, inflation remained above central bank targets, and markets wavered, fueling concerns that the long stretch of US economic growth might be coming to an end. Those turbulent headlines drove market volatility, with the S&P 500 ® Index dropping almost into correction territory in the first quarter of 2026. This report assumes that the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed until late May, with shipping traffic beginning to pick up in June. Oil shipments through the strait, however, will not likely reach pre-conflict levels until later this year, and we expect some oil production in the Middle East to remain disrupted over that period.
